subject: science
passage: Ice cores drilled from the Greenland ice sheet, some of them more than three kilometers ______ hold a record of the atmosphere that stretches back more than 100,000 years. As snow piled up each winter and was pressed into ice, tiny bubbles of air were sealed inside it. By melting a slice of core in a vacuum and measuring the gases that escape, researchers can read the level of carbon dioxide in the air at the time the snow fell, and the visible layers let them count the years, much as rings record the age of a tree.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: "Some of them more than three kilometers long" is extra information about the ice cores. It opens with a comma after "sheet," so it must close with a comma before the verb "hold."
explanation.A: Correct. The closing comma matches the opening comma after "sheet" and completes the pair around the extra information.
explanation.B: Incorrect. A semicolon can't separate the subject "Ice cores" from its verb "hold."
explanation.C: Incorrect. Without a closing comma, the extra information is never set off and runs straight into the verb "hold."
explanation.D: Incorrect. The extra information opens with a comma, so it can't close with a dash; the two marks must match.
